children: There's a flood of communication coming from the Reserve Bank of Australia next week, but one event stands out. Attention will be on remarks on Wednesday by Andrew Hauser, deputy governor of the RBA. Hauser likes to speak plainly, which is welcomed by traders as they try to assess the outlook for monetary policy. Hauser was clearly sending hawkish messages prior to the RBA's last interest-rate rise in September, highlighting the anger in the community that inflation has remained elevated for too long. So there will be a lot of eyeballs on him as he looks again at the economy. (james.glynn@wsj.com; @JamesGlynnWSJ)
